input: scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products

doc_friction.issue: shift-roster-builder's next: is at the 2000-character cap and mostly optimiser micro-items on synthetic 300-person weeks; product items for the real 5-20 person customer (proof-of-presence clock, onboarding) were not listed, so allocate.py steers runs toward low-user-value perf work

deviations.why: The row's buildable items (a 4 s repair reserve at 300+ copies, a warm-sized gate) speed up 300-person synthetic weeks for a product whose users are 5-20 person teams. Closing the time clock's honour-system gap (buddy punching, off-site punches) is a feature competitors charge for and a reason a small business would pick the hub, so it was worth more per hour.
deviations.did: Built optional per-person clock PINs with a lockout and a distance-only site geofence instead of the listed optimiser items
deviations.result: Landed with 5 tests and a headless-Chromium run; flagships next now lists it

notes: Added clockguard.mjs (PBKDF2 PIN hashing via Web Crypto so it runs on the Worker; 5-try/15-min lock with HTTP 429; haversine geofence storing only metres + phone accuracy; flag or block mode) and wired it into hub.mjs (team-page PIN box, geolocation script, /admin/pin, timesheet section) and timeclock.mjs (punch.where, place flags in timesheet and CSV). Checked: node --test clockguard.test.mjs timeclock.test.mjs pass (5 new tests); a Playwright run of the real page with a granted location 67 m from the site stored {m:67,acc:20,away:false}, and with location not granted the punch still reached the server. Full venture suite and venture-preflight results are in the PR body. Not tried on a real phone at a real site.
